ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 5622, as amended; Yuhan Hoesa provisions under Articles 543 through 613), Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 15761, as amended), Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Registration Act, Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 18795, as amended), Financial Transactions Reports Act (FTRA, Act No. 18642, as amended), Presidential Decree No. 32818 under the FTRA, Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality (Act No. 17430, as amended), and the Supreme Court Registration Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain certified copy of registered corporate matters from the Korean District Court Commercial Registry, notarize the underlying authorization if required, obtain Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, and do not request consular legalization because Korea is an Apostille Convention Contracting State; for documents originating outside Korea, use notarization, then Apostille from the competent authority of the origin state, and never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or corporate registry authority in the jurisdiction of origin of each material shareholder or corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certificate in the country of origin, attach Apostille issued by the designated competent authority under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, obtain certified English or Korean sworn translation, and do not add Korean consular legalization unless the origin state is not party to the Apostille Convention, in which case use the parallel route of local authentication followed by Korean Embassy or Consulate legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent entity or Ultimate Beneficial Owner, or initial members of the proposed Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute before a notary public, have the notary certificate attached, obtain Apostille from the competent authority of the state where executed, submit with a certified Korean translation to the Korean incorporation counsel; if the executing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state, use local notarization, local foreign ministry authentication, then Korean consular legalization as the exclusive route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial members of the Yuhan Hoesa and Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Prepare in Korean, execute by all initial members, notarize at a Korean notary office, obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for any use in another Convention Contracting State, and do not apply for Korean consular legalization because the Apostille is sufficient and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate bank maintaining the account of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner or foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead with banker's signature, notarize the signature in the issuing state, obtain Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state, attach sworn Korean translation for submission to Korean banks and tax authorities, and if the issuing state is not an Apostille Convention member, use the separate consular legalization path through the Korean diplomatic mission in that state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration and Source of Wealth Statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each natural person who directly or indirectly owns or controls 25 percent or more of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign before a Korean notary or foreign notary, obtain Apostille from the notary's competent authority, attach certified Korean translation, and treat the document as Government_Only_Access for submission to Korean financial institutions, tax authorities, and KoFIU rather than any public filing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, Ultimate Beneficial Owners, directors, and authorized signatories must be screened at engagement and at least annually against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, Republic of Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and domestic government sanctions lists, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions as best practice, and global financial intelligence PEP and adverse media databases. Each hit must require enhanced due diligence, independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, documentation of family and business relationships, and escalation to the AML compliance officer with consideration of a Suspicious Transaction Report to KoFIU under the Financial Transactions Reports Act. Screening must be refreshed before any Stripe or Apple IAP payment rail activation and upon any 10 percent ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-Register) operated jointly with the Model Registration Office of the competent District Court
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal form suffix must be expressed in Korean as Yuhan Hoesa and the registered commercial name must be written in Korean Hangul characters; a parallel English name may be used as an auxiliary transliteration, but the statutory name clearance is based on Hangul distinguishability. The four-tier naming convention is, in order, descriptive industry token, distinctive brand or house name, transliterated foreign brand where appropriate, and the Yuhan Hoesa legal form suffix. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an already registered commercial name in the same business class when compared on a spelling and phonetic basis.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registry will state the precise legal ground and the applicant s counsel should immediately request the written refusal. The applicant must then file a written appeal against the refusal with the registration officer within the statutory two-week window, asking for reconsideration and supplying three to five alternative names with formal distinguishability analysis. If the registration officer affirms the refusal, counsel must file an immediate appeal to the registration division of the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Civil Case Litigation Procedure Act, attaching the original clearance search, the relevant Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Act provisions, and a legal memorandum proving that the rejected name is not misleading, not identical, and not within a prohibited token category. Payment of registration tax should be withheld until final acceptance of the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox will not satisfy the principal office and business substance requirements of the Korean Commercial Act, and the Korean local tax office will generally reject a virtual mailbox as the proper corporate and VAT registration address for an active fintech software company. For an online personal wealth analytics application processing subscription and IAP revenue, a serviced or co-working office with a physical business suite, meeting room access, employee workspace, corporate signage, mail handling, and a formal commercial lease may be accepted. Major Korean banks will require a physical commercial address for corporate account opening and will reject PO boxes and standalone virtual office addresses. The arrangement should also support the preparation of Korean tax invoices, financial records, data server access logs, and records of the physical place where core management decisions are made.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 10 to 20 percent over the first three years for a low-risk fintech entity using a properly documented physical co-working office in Seoul; the risk rises to 60 to 80 percent if only a virtual office or commercial mailbox is used and Stripe or Apple IAP revenues are booked without a proper Korean tax and corporate substance infrastructure. Inspection checklist: (1) current commercial lease or service agreement for a dedicated physical workspace; (2) company name signboard at the registered address; (3) physical workplace or workstation capacity consistent with declared operations; (4) accessible corporate records, tax invoices, and accounting ledgers; (5) data and server access logs; (6) compliance screening records for beneficial owners; and (7) no indicator that the registered address is a residential mailbox or postal forwarding point without any actual business presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Act No. 1000, as most recently amended; principally Articles 543 (formation of limited liability company), Article 553 (members' contribution and paid-in capital), Article 560 (articles of incorporation), and Article 562 (organization and registration of the company). Supplementary application of the Framework Act on National Taxes for registration stamp duty and the Corporate Income Tax Act for entity-level taxation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, and the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea for electronic filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관), Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (유한회사설립등기신청서), and Certificate of Incorporation (등기사항전부증명서).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. Capital is freely determined by the members and must be fully contributed before or at the time of registration. No blocked escrow account is required unless voluntarily specified in the articles of incorporation or imposed by a financial-services regulator.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE FOUNDING MEMBERS AND INITIAL DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA, a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. The undersigned, being all of the founding members and the initial directors of the company, do hereby waive formal notice and convene in person on this ____ day of __________, 20____, at the registered office of the company. The chairperson confirms that all directors and all founding members are present, that a quorum exists under Article 560 of the Commercial Act and the company's Articles of Incorporation, and that this meeting is duly constituted to transact corporate business. After due deliberation, the following resolutions are unanimously adopted and declared immediately effective. FIRST, the share capital of the company is fixed at [insert Korean Won amount], divided into [insert number] fully paid membership units. Each member's contribution has been received and credited in full to the company's bank account, and the directors are authorized to execute any receipt, certificate, or ledger entry evidencing such payment. SECOND, the registered office of the company is adopted as the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, and the directors are authorized to file any notice of commencement or change thereof with the competent registry office and tax authorities. THIRD, the directors named in the Articles of Incorporation are confirmed as the initial board of directors, and the following officers are elected and appointed: the chairperson of the board, the chief executive officer, and any other officers whose titles are listed in these resolutions. Each officer is vested with authority to manage ordinary business affairs, to open and maintain bank accounts, to execute contracts and digital service agreements, and to make tax filings. FOURTH, the banking authorization is granted to the chief executive officer and to any director designated by him or her, jointly or severally, to open, operate, and close bank accounts with any licensed financial institution in the Republic of Korea, and to execute checks, wire transfer instructions, payment processor mandates, and electronic banking authorizations on behalf of the company. FIFTH, the directors are directed to complete all filings required for corporate income tax registration, value-added tax registration, and registration with the National Tax Service, and to obtain any business licenses, statutory permissions, or certificate of seal registration necessary for the company to conduct its lawful business. SIXTH, the directors and officers are authorized to adopt a corporate seal, to certify officer signatures, to prepare and file the statutory registration application, and to take any other actions necessary or desirable to perfect incorporation and commence business. Finally, the secretary of the meeting is directed to prepare a written record of these resolutions, which shall be preserved in the corporate minute book and deemed effective upon the filing of the company's certificate of incorporation. Adopted and approved by unanimous consent of the directors and founding members this ____ day of __________, 20____.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local notary public (공증인) authorized under the Notary Public Act and the Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding members must convene and approve the Articles of Incorporation. The articles must include the company's corporate name, object clause describing the digital financial-portfolio-tracking business, address of the registered office, total issued membership units and contribution value, names and resident registration numbers of members, and names of initial directors. Under Article 560 of the Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa may adopt a simplified governance structure but must appoint at least one director who is an individual. Submit the drafted Korean-language articles to the notary together with each member's identification and a power of attorney if any member acts through an agent. The notary will verify legal capacity and notarize execution. The notarized articles are mandatory for the registration application.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Valid passport or national ID of each founder
Power of attorney if a founder is not appearing in person
Proof of address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses or queries the submission, correct the articles to conform to mandatory provisions of Articles 560 through 564 of the Commercial Act, file a revised draft, and pay any additional notarial fee. If founder identity or authority is questioned, submit apostilled or consularized identification and a formal power of attorney. If the notary raises substantive legal issues, retain Korean counsel to issue a supplementary legal opinion for the notary's file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Registration with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, or the Electronic Filing Portal of the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation with the competent registry office. The application must be accompanied by the notarized articles of incorporation, certificate of paid-in capital, and written consent or certificate of appointment of directors and the statutory auditor if any. Filing may be made in person at the court registration window or electronically through the internet registration system. The registry officer will verify the application, the legal compliance of the object clause, the adequacy of the company name, and the jurisdiction of the registered office. After verification, the officer will assign a commercial registration number, record the company in the register, and issue the Certificate of Incorporation and certified corporate seal registration certificate if a seal is registered.
required_dossiers: Certificate of payment of capital or bank certificate of received contribution
Power of attorney if filing by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of correction or suspension, cure each identified defect within the 15-day statutory correction period by submitting an amended application and supplementary documents. If the name is rejected due to conflict with an identical or confusingly similar existing corporation, select a new name and file an amended application. If a judge raises concerns about lack of a statutory representative, promptly appoint a compliant director and file proof of such appointment. If the correction period lapses, file a new application; the original filing fee may be retained by the court and a new filing fee is due.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the National Tax Service and Local Tax Offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office, and the relevant municipal revenue office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the commercial registration certificate, the company must apply for business registration for the purpose of income tax, corporate tax, value-added tax, and local taxes. The applicant shall furnish the company's certificate of incorporation, sealed copy of articles, corporate seal certificate, and office lease agreement. Because the entity will perform an ISIC 6201 digital portfolio tracking service, the officer must select the appropriate business code for software and data processing services and indicate that the business is a taxable digital service subject to the electronic tax invoice obligation. The tax office will assign a business registration number, confirming the entity-level tax status. The company must then register for the electronic tax invoice system, register its corporate seal, and file an opening report with the local tax office for property and local income tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Copy of registration information from the court
Lease agreement or proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a correction request, update the classification code, representative details, or office address and resubmit the application. If the electronic tax invoice registration is delayed, apply through the Hometax portal manually; an administrative appeal may be filed with the National Tax Service within 90 days if the office rejects a tax classification requested by the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Activate Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea acting under the Banking Act, and the Financial Supervisory Service for anti-money-laundering compliance of the bank's account-opening process
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must open a corporate bank account to fund the paid-in capital and to operate the digital payment rails. The representative director or an appointed officer must appear at the bank with the corporate seal, certificate of incorporation, certified copy of business registration, articles of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, and documents proving the identity and beneficial ownership of the members and persons with significant control. Since the business is an ISIC 6201 personal wealth analytics platform using Stripe and Apple IAP, the bankers may require a description of the business model, planned transaction volume, and a copy of the privacy policy or financial information protection protocol. The bank will perform customer due diligence under the Financial Transactions Reports Act before activating the account. After the account is opened, the company may sign agreements with payment service providers and submit its Korean tax invoice registration to Stripe and Apple.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of the representative director
Proof of beneficial ownership and ultimate beneficial owner declaration
Board resolution approving the bank account and payment processors
Detailed business description and projected transaction volume
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening for enhanced due diligence, the company shall provide the requested beneficial ownership chart, financial statements, or source-of-funds declaration. If the bank rejects the application because the business involves fintech portfolio tracking, the company may apply to another licensed bank, or amend the business description to clarify that the company provides software analytics and does not hold or intermediate client funds. If the rejection is unjustified, file a complaint with the Financial Supervisory Service's complaint portal or request mediation under the Act on the Protection of Financial Consumers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the registered business scope is ISIC 6201 (computer programming, data processing and related activities), a non-industrial digital service that does not require an Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. No physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity is licensed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, air pollutant emissions, VOCs, or hazardous waste generation arise from the digital portfolio tracking service.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical premises are engaged in manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing activity; accordingly, no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection under the Civil Defense Act, or occupational safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is triggered for the ISIC 6201 software service. The company shall nevertheless comply with ordinary commercial building fire safety requirements in its office lease.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax (http://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must appoint a domestic tax agent (tax manager) resident in South Korea and file a Business Registration Application with the local district tax office having jurisdiction over that tax agent's place of business, either in person or through the HomeTax electronic portal. Required attachments include an apostilled or notarized original of the foreign business registration certificate, articles of incorporation or equivalent constitutive documents, a resolution appointing the local tax agent, a power of attorney, and a certified copy of the tax agent's identification. The NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as both the corporate tax reference and the VAT registration number, normally within 3 to 5 business days. There is no minimum share capital requirement for this registration process. The tax agent must maintain the registration and discharge all ongoing VAT, corporate income tax, and withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box regime in the US sense. A Yuhan Hoesa formed under the Commercial Act is treated as a domestic corporation for Korean tax purposes, subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income, with no elective pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold. All business operators, whether resident or non-resident, making taxable supplies in South Korea are required to register for VAT with the National Tax Service. For small business operators with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million, the Simplified Taxpayer regime applies (VAT effectively calculated as 2% of turnover), but registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic Tax Invoice (e-Tax Invoice) transmission via HomeTax is mandatory. All registered taxpayers must issue and transmit an electronic tax invoice through HomeTax no later than the day following the supply date. The system supports NTS-specified API and XML interoperability, but there is no real-time pre-clearance fiscal stamping mechanism as found in certain Latin American jurisdictions. Fraud controls rely on mandatory e-invoice reconciliation, data matching, and the ability of the NTS to demand digital yet detailed supply records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim 0% export zero-rating under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act, the taxpayer must substantiate: (i) for goods, physical exportation from South Korea evidenced by a valid Korean Customs Service export declaration; or (ii) for services, provision to a non-resident client for use or consumption outside South Korea, with the consideration received in freely convertible foreign currency and repatriated into South Korea through an authorized foreign exchange bank. For the relevant business scope (ISIC 6201, cloud-based personal wealth analytics and investment tracking software), qualifying exports include cross-border software-as-a-service subscriptions and digital content services delivered to non-resident users, provided the services are effectively used outside South Korea and the requisite documentary evidence is retained. Domestic B2B digital supplies remain standard-rated at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) issued by the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement
Commercial Invoice and underlying contract or service order
Inward Remittance Certificate or Certificate of Foreign Exchange Settlement issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank
Digital service delivery records, including user location logs and download or access receipts for electronically supplied services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to periodic NTS desk and field audits. If the required supporting documentation, including the export declaration, transport evidence, and foreign exchange settlement certificate within the 180-day repatriation deadline, is missing, incomplete, or false, the NTS will reverse the zero-rating application and assess VAT at 10% of the supply value, plus additional tax penalties of at least 50% of the amount evaded for negligent non-compliance and up to 100% for deliberate fraud. Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, responsible executives may face criminal liability with imprisonment up to five years or fines up to KRW 100 million. Retrospective clawback periods generally extend to 10 years for fraudulent or willful non-disclosure and 5 years for ordinary unreported under-assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a highly open current account and a substantially liberalized capital account, with the Korean won generally convertible for trade, service payments, and legitimate profit remittance through authorized foreign exchange banks. Current account settlements for software subscriptions, app-store receivables, and cross-border service fees do not require a prior license, but must be processed through a domestic foreign exchange bank and reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injection into a Yuhan Hoesa and the subsequent repatriation of dividends or liquidation proceeds, are classified as capital transactions and require a BOK/MOEF foreign exchange transaction report submitted by the receiving bank. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted, but banks require proof of corporate tax withholding, audited financial statements, the certificate of business registration, and documentary evidence that the underlying investment capital was lawfully brought into South Korea. Practical constraints include mandatory beneficial ownership disclosure, strict source-of-funds verification for foreign investors, and the need for the remitter to identify a valid foreign exchange purpose code; failure to present complete documentation can delay inward remittance and capital verification. Although no general surrender requirement exists, foreign exchange banks must still ensure that all capital inflows are traced to a stated legitimate economic purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, Korean exporters, including software and fintech entities, must collect export proceeds through a domestic foreign exchange bank within 6 months from the date of export, unless an extension is approved by the designated bank or by the BOK/MOEF. There is no mandatory conversion to Korean won and no statutory surrender ratio to the central bank; exporters may lawfully retain foreign currency receipts in eligible foreign currency deposit accounts. However, all export proceeds must pass through an authorized foreign exchange bank for trade reporting and cross-border reconciliation, with the underlying export settlement method and payment details recorded in the Foreign Exchange Information System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise or Revolut Business do not hold a South Korean electronic financial payment service provider license and are legally barred from providing domestic KRW current accounts or local clearing services for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. They may only offer auxiliary non-KRW accounts or card products and cannot serve as the primary banking relationship for capital verification, foreign exchange reporting, or statutory corporate treasury management. A domestic Tier-1 commercial bank is mandatory for opening the operational currency account and capital escrow account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In the standard onboarding process for a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with foreign non-resident ownership, the statutory director and beneficial owners must generally appear physically at a South Korean commercial bank branch for an identity and business purpose interview. Remote or consular proxy opening is not a guaranteed right; it is accepted only at the banks discretion if an apostilled power of attorney, certified passport copies, corporate registration documents, and a consular-verified identity certificate are provided. For a low-risk fintech software entity, some banks permit a video-call interview after the initial physical visit, but a physical presence mandate remains the safest assumption for treasury planning.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder funds wired in for share capital without a clear ownership trail, especially if the transferring entity is offshore or newly incorporated
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles of incorporation, corporate register, a complete UBO declaration form for every direct and indirect shareholder holding 25% or more, 6-month source-of-funds bank statements from the transferring entity, passport copies apostilled, a source-of-wealth narrative, share subscription agreement, and a board resolution authorizing the capital transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank AML compliance misclassifies the Financial Portfolio Tracking scope as investment advisory or client-fund custody under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written legal opinion from Korean securities counsel stating that the product is a non-discretionary financial data analytics application, the company does not hold client funds, revenue derives exclusively from SaaS subscriptions and app-store commissions, and no investment recommendation or portfolio execution service is performed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign exchange purpose code mismatch or incomplete documentation on the inbound investment wire, causing the receiving bank to file a suspicious transaction report
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed foreign exchange transaction declaration classified as capital transaction for acquisition of domestic company shares, the banks inward remittance confirmation, the certificate of foreign direct investment report, a forward-looking business plan, proforma invoices for expected app revenue, and the companys foreign exchange bank declaration form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Enhanced due diligence triggered by the software fintech profile and the foreign majority ownership, leading to false-positive sanctions hits or concerns about exposure to crypto-linked payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening certificates from a reputable compliance aggregator, clear beneficial-owner screening results against OFAC/UN/EU/DPRK lists, a written representation that no counterparty or vendor is located in or controlled from North Korea, a company AML policy, proof that all revenues are collected via regulated Stripe and Apple IAP rails, and a formal statement that crypto assets are not accepted or traded.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection for the Yuhan Hoesa must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder to the designated Korean foreign exchange bank, with the remittance instruction clearly referencing the FETA capital transaction purpose code for acquisition of domestic company shares. The receiving bank will verify the share subscription, press the remittance into the capital escrow account, and submit the mandatory foreign exchange transaction report to the BOK/MOEF through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Capital verification is evidenced by the banks inward remittance certificate, the paid-in capital receipt, the foreign direct investment declaration, and an entry in the share register showing issuance of limited liability shares to the non-resident member.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and operational outflows, the entity should use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for vendor payments, SaaS infrastructure fees, cloud service settlements, and contractor disbursements. Commercial letters of credit are available through Tier-1 Korean banks for physical goods or hardware procurement, while documentary collections can be used for lower-value trade transactions. Inbound customer collection from the software product remains on Stripe and Apple IAP settlement channels; those funds settle into the domestic KRW account, and the company then reprices and manages operating disbursements through its Korean foreign exchange bank as the primary clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD trade-related forward contracts with real underlying service or goods exposure, executed through a domestic Korean foreign exchange bank

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for offshore hedging of Korean won exposure, permitted only for customers without a domestic hedging license and not as a primary onshore tool for the Korean entity
Onshore plain-vanilla currency swaps for eligible capital flows, dividend repatriation, and large cross-border settlements, subject to MOEF reporting thresholds and evidence of real demand
Foreign currency deposit-based natural hedging using retained USD receipts to offset future USD vendor payments, with no speculative leverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (including audited financial statements attachment, international transaction report, and tax adjustment entries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year filers; otherwise within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or underpaid corporate tax attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid amount (or 10% for unintentional omission) plus statutory overdue interest of approximately 0.022% per day under the Framework Act on National Taxes. If tax is fraudulently underreported, the penalty escalates to 40% of the unpaid amount. Continuous non-filing may trigger tax seizure and a court-ordered administrative strike-off under Commercial Act dormant-company rules after five consecutive years of inactive filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim Corporate Income Tax Prepayment Return (mid-term tax payment for the first half of the fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By August 31 of the current fiscal year for calendar-year taxpayers (within 2 months after the first six months of the fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay interim corporate tax incurs an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid interim amount, plus daily overdue interest at 0.022% per day. Nonpayment may lead to immediate seizure schedules and attachment orders without a separate demand notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Local Income Tax Return and Payment (local surtax on corporate income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered office (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government) via WETAX e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 of the year following the fiscal year-end (within 1 month after the corporate income tax return deadline); for calendar-year filers, April 30 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent local income tax is subject to an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid amount and local tax delinquency charges of 0.75% per month up to a cap of 75% of the unpaid tax. Long-term non-filing permits the local government to impose coercive collection measures including asset garnishment and can result in an administrative disposition that effectively closes the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim Local Income Tax Return and Payment (semi-annual local surtax prepayment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered office via WETAX
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By September 30 of the current fiscal year for calendar-year filers (within 1 month after the interim corporate tax return deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interim local income tax payments accrue the same 20% additional tax and monthly local delinquency charges, with enforcement including wage and bank account attachments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Company Status Report (annual UBO and foreign shareholding confirmation under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the competent foreign exchange bank, transmitted to the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each fiscal year (by January 30 for calendar-year companies; anniversary rule for off-calendar fiscal years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign-invested status report subjects the company to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,846) under FIPA Article 29; repeated non-filing can result in cancellation of foreign-invested status, losing statutory foreign-investor protections and tax-related incentives after formal order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report Filing (for entities meeting mandatory audit thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through the DART electronic disclosure system; a copy delivered to the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks from the date of the auditor's report; the report must be obtained before the statutory deadline for the annual general meeting and corporate tax return (i.e., before March 31 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company required to undergo an external audit that fails to appoint an auditor or file the audit report may be fined up to KRW 50,000,000 (approx. USD 38,462); the FSC may ask the Securities and Futures Commission to appoint an auditor ex officio at the company's expense, and the corporate tax return may be treated as defective, triggering audit tax reassessment and refusal of fiscal loss carryforwards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By July 25 of the current fiscal year for the taxable period from January 1 to June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT filing or underdeclaration incurs an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid VAT, plus daily overdue interest at 0.022% per day. False tax invoices can trigger criminal penalties and business registration revocation in severe cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 25 of the following fiscal year for the taxable period from July 1 to December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT filing or underdeclaration incurs an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid VAT, plus daily overdue interest at 0.022% per day. False tax invoices can trigger criminal penalties and business registration revocation in severe cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory external audit is compulsory under the Korean External Audit Act (Act on External Audit and Accounting) for: (1) any corporation (including a Yuhan Hoesa) whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million); (2) a company with total assets of KRW 10 billion or more that is additionally designated by the Financial Services Commission due to high leverage or public interest; (3) all securities-listed companies regardless of asset size; and (4) companies designated by the FSC because they are investment companies, state-invested entities, or operate in manner that compromises public interest. No revenue or headcount trigger applies under the External Audit Act; only total assets and regulatory designation are relevant. Small- and medium-sized venture enterprises may be exempt only when a statutory auditor provides an exemption opinion in accordance with applicable rules, but if the exemption is not exercised, a certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants must conduct the audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatorily applied by listed companies and by entities designated as external audit subjects under the Act on External Audit and Accounting. Non-public Yuhan Hoesa entities that are not required to apply K-IFRS may use the Korean General Enterprise Accounting Standards (K-GAAP) or the SME Accounting Standards if total assets remain below KRW 12 billion, provided the chosen framework is applied consistently. All external audit engagements must follow Korean Auditing Standards (KSA) issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no general annual UBO confirmation filing at the Korean commercial registry for a Yuhan Hoesa, but two statutory confirmation duties apply: (i) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, every foreign-invested company must annually report the current foreign investment status, including beneficial ownership percentages, amount contributed, and nationality of ultimate beneficial owners, within 30 days after fiscal year-end; and (ii) under the Commercial Act, any transfer of an equity interest (equity unit) in a Yuhan Hoesa must be registered in the company's register of members and, for a transfer requiring approval, a resolution of the general meeting of members must be obtained. Changes in foreign shareholding percentages must additionally be reported to the competent exchange bank or authority within 30 days after the underlying share transfer or capital change; failure to update the commercial registry within 14 days after such change results in a penalty charged by the court registrar. An annual written confirmation of UBO status should be obtained from all members holding 10% or more and attached to the annual audit file where the audit threshold is met.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive national corporate income tax brackets in South Korea: 9% up to KRW 200m; 19% from KRW 200m to KRW 20bn; 21% from KRW 20bn to KRW 300bn; 24% above KRW 300bn. A 10% local income tax surcharge is imposed on the national tax due, producing a combined top marginal effective rate of approximately 26.4%. For the Yuhan Hoesa LLC, statutory incentives available include the Special Tax Treatment Control Law (STTCL) R&D tax credits (up to 50% of qualified R&D expenditure for progressively expansible IT/SAAS development), tax deductions for capital investment in technology, foreign direct investment tax deferral, venture SME income tax reductions, and free economic zone tax holidays. No separate patent box exists, but beneficial R&D credits and loss-carryforward mechanics operate favorably.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Form #CIT-5 - '법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서' / Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (by 31 March for a December 31 year-end). A one-month extension is available upon application. Quarterly interim prepayment declarations are also required within 2 months after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the tax accounting period (YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD). For Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory fiscal year is the calendar year unless a different fiscal year has been formally registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC must use the period registered at the Korean tax office. Even if a foreign parent operates on a different fiscal year, the Korean return cannot be consolidated or aligned without pre-approval. A non-resident investor should ensure that the Korean entity maintains separate audited books for the calendar year to avoid penalty for inconsistent reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Corporate Identification and Capital Structure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter business registration number, legal entity name (Yuhan Hoesa LLC), registered address, representative director, business activity code (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210), and the schedule of shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all non-resident shareholders with their foreign tax identification numbers and ownership percentages. If a non-resident owns directly or indirectly more than 50%, the entity is a foreign-invested enterprise and must file foreign investment disclosures under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Failure to declare ultimate beneficial ownership for international tax compliance triggers separate administrative penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record total gross operating revenue from all business sources: subscription fees, financial portfolio tracking software sales, SaaS hosting, IAP revenue from Apple/Stripe, licensing, and maintenance services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue must be booked gross in Korean Won (KRW). For app store sales, include the full customer-facing sales amount as revenue and report the platform commission (Apple/Stripe fee) as a deductible selling expense. Foreign currency sales must be converted at the transaction-date exchange rate; Korean GAAP revenue recognition rules apply. Cross-border payments routed through payment aggregators should not be netted, and underreporting of gross IAP revenue is a primary audit flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter operating deductions: payroll, social insurance, cloud hosting, data licensing, software development, marketing, app-store commission, depreciation, and amortization, along with a schedule of non-deductible items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean LLC pays royalties, interest, or management service fees to any foreign related party, the deduction is limited to an arm's length amount and requires proper withholding tax treatment. Expense invoices from non-resident vendors must be accompanied by evidence that withholding tax was either deducted or treaty relief was obtained. A deduction may also be denied if the vendor lacks economic substance or withholds no documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable Income Reconciliation and Add-Backs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile gross profit to taxable income by adding back disallowed expenses (entertainment over statutory limits, non-statutory penalties, capital losses) and subtracting exempt income or deferred items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividends, foreign capital gains from an overseas subsidiary, and other foreign-source income must be segregated. Direct foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income are available as a foreign tax credit, but only if the proper Korean foreign tax credit limitation schedule is attached. A non-resident shareholder's personal tax position does not affect the Korean entity-level calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter unused net operating loss carryforwards deducted in the current tax year. Pursuant to Korean Corporate Income Tax Act Article 13 and its amendment, losses may be carried forward 15 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean tax law does not impose a continuity-of-ownership test unless the loss carryforward is used in an aggressive anti-avoidance arrangement. If ownership was changed during the year, prepare documentation supporting business purpose and substance. Failure to maintain loss carryforward schedules can lead to denial by the National Tax Service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax Base and Progressive Rate Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive tax table to the taxable base (after NOL and deductions). For tax years beginning after 2023: 9% up to KRW 200m, 19% over KRW 200m, 21% over KRW 20bn, 24% over KRW 300bn.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Since Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic entity, it is taxed on worldwide income. Income from a foreign permanent establishment is assessed under the same progressive schedule but may be entitled to foreign tax credit and the Korean participation exemption for capital gains. The non-resident shareholder must not compute the entity's tax base; the Korean LLC itself files the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtract foreign tax credits, R&D credits, venture investment credits, job creation credits, withholding credits, interim quarterly prepayments, and other refundable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit schedule must be filed along with proof of foreign tax liability. For a Korean LLC receiving dividends from a foreign subsidiary, indirect foreign tax credit may be available if the direct ownership exceeds a specific threshold, but the claim must be substantiated by overseas tax returns. Interim prepayments paid by the Korean LLC are credited here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the final amount of corporate income tax due after credits, prepayments, and surcharge. This amount is paid to the National Tax Service through HomeTax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC must make the final payment by the statutory deadline. If a refund is claimed, the Korean bank account must be designated. If the LLC has not paid the tax due, the National Tax Service may deny the issuance of a tax clearance certificate and blacklist the entity, and the foreign parent's remittance could be blocked under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Corporate Income Tax Return by the statutory deadline results in a negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax (or 10% if filed late but before assessment). Underreporting taxable income by mistake triggers a 10% understatement penalty, while fraudulent underreporting triggers a 30% penalty (and up to 40% in certain severe cases) under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Late payments additionally accrue daily overdue surcharges of 0.022% per day from the due date (maximum 9% of the unpaid amount). Willful failure to file can also constitute criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 5 years or fines not exceeding three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15.4% (14% national corporate income tax withheld at source plus 1.4% local income tax surcharge) on gross dividends paid by the Korean LLC to a non-resident corporate shareholder, unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Treaty (DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the jurisdiction of residence; (2) submit to the Korean withholding agent a written 'Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty' together with the TRC and a beneficial ownership statement proving that the recipient is the true economic owner and not a conduit, shell, or pass-through vehicle; (3) provide evidence of the shareholding percentage, detailed legal basis, and, if required, a limitation on benefits analysis; and (4) file the foreign transaction report with the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank. The withholding agent must comply before withholding at the reduced treaty rate, and any excess withholding must be refunded by filing a refund claim with the National Tax Service within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by the Korean LLC to a non-resident for software patents, trademarks, know-how, or other intellectual property are subject to statutory withholding tax of 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge). Interest paid to a non-resident on intercompany loans or debentures is subject to statutory withholding of 15.4% (14% national tax plus 1.4% local surcharge). Under OECD-compliant Double Tax Treaties, the rates are frequently reduced to 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, and dividends to 5% or 10% for qualified substantial-ownership shareholders. The treaty relief is conditional upon filing the TRC, satisfying the beneficial ownership test, and adhering to the anti-abuse provisions under the LOB and principal purpose test.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when the aggregate annual amount of cross-border related-party transactions (goods, services, loans, royalties) exceeds KRW 50 billion. Master File is required when the consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion. Even below these thresholds, the National Tax Service may require contemporaneous documentation for transfer pricing audits based on the substance of the Korean LLC's cross-border transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply the UAE's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to this Yuhan Hoesa LLC, but the Korean tax system applies the substance-over-form doctrine, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the special anti-abuse provisions under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The National Tax Service will require actual management and operational substance in Korea for the cloud-based financial portfolio tracking business, including staff, office, decision-making functions, and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA). If the Korean entity is merely a paper shell directing profits to a foreign related party, the NTS will disregard the entity and re-characterize income, deny treaty benefits, and impose tax on the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Intentional Underreporting of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC deliberately omits gross revenues derived from Apple IAP, Stripe settlement, and financial portfolio tracking subscription fees; fabricates transaction records; inflates expenses through fake overseas cloud service invoices; or claims fictitious R&D tax credits for software development activities that do not qualify.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (Articles 3 and 9), intentional tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years, or a fine equal to three times the evaded tax amount. In addition, the National Tax Service imposes a fraud understatement penalty of 30% to 40% of the underpaid tax, plus monthly late surcharges and prohibited tax clearance. The case is also subject to criminal referral to the Supreme Prosecutor's Office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil of the Yuhan Hoesa LLC is pierceable where the director used the LLC as a mere alter ego to conceal revenue. The director is then jointly and severally liable for the full corporate tax underpayment, penalties, and interest. The NTS may impose a travel ban (blacklisting) prohibiting the director from leaving Korea until the outstanding liability is settled, and the director faces criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years and civil restitution in the amount of taxes avoided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Substance Grafting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC charges royalties or management fees to a foreign subsidiary for software licenses that were actually developed in Korea; makes intercompany loans with artificially low interest rates; or routes financial analytics contracts to a low-tax shell jurisdiction while the Korean staff and management perform all Core Income-Generating Activities, without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (Article 6), the NTS may re-determine taxable income based on the arm's length principle and impose an additional income adjustment penalty of 10% of the corrected amount. If failure to file the TP report is determined after audit, separate administrative fines apply, and the deductibility of the mispriced royalties and interest is disallowed in full, resulting in a higher taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved the false intercompany contracts can be held personally liable for the resulting corporate tax deficiency under the principle of negligent supervisor liability. If intentional transfer pricing manipulation is shown, the director is subject to criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may be forced to provide personal assets for recovery. In flagrant cases, the director is blacklisted and banned from overseas travel until payment is made; civil damages may be claimed by minority shareholders or the bankrupt estate under the Commercial Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Illegal Outbound Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa LLC is operated as a pure shell in Korea with no office, no staff, and no accounting substance, while all financial portfolio tracking revenue is immediately distributed as dividends, loans, or sham service fees to a non-resident affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction, without any real holding period, commercial purpose, or DTA claim; the entity also fails to file Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting for outbound remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service and the Bank of Korea jointly may characterize the Korean LLC as a sham under the substance-over-form doctrine. The full outbound flow is treated as constructive dividend or additional taxable income for the Korean entity, WHT is recaptured at the statutory rate, and a penalty of up to 20% of the transaction amount may be imposed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Criminal referral for unauthorized monetary defense or fraud is possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate form is disregarded where a mere shell is used to evade corporate tax or foreign exchange controls. Directors are personally liable for unpaid withholding taxes, corporate income taxes, and currency control penalties. They are subject to exit (travel) bans and the NTS tax delinquent blacklisting system. In serious cases, the director may be convicted of fraud under the Criminal Code and sentenced to up to 10 years' imprisonment, with restitution of the fully dispersed and reinvested funds.
